PR #42 (closed): refresh bug fix
Hello,

First of all, thank you for the todo project you've developed. As a JavaScript beginner, I've found it incredibly beneficial. However, during testing, I encountered a bug related to handling todos with identical content in the data source. Specifically, when attempting to delete a todo item, the absence of a mapping between components and records can lead to a disorder upon refresh. Here's how the bug can be reproduced:

Initially, we add eight todo items in the following order: aa, bb, cc, dd, aa, bb, cc, dd. At this point, the todoList records are as follows: {"todo":["aa","bb","cc","dd","aa","bb","cc","dd"],"completed":[]}

If we try to delete (or complete) the fifth record (aa), the page directly manipulates the DOM to remove the item. Consequently, the todo records on the page from bottom to top become aa, bb, cc, dd, bb, cc, dd. Although this seems correct, the actual todoList records become {"todo":["bb","cc","dd","aa","bb","cc","dd"],"completed":[]}.

This discrepancy occurs because the operation data.todo.splice(data.todo.indexOf(value), 1) deletes the first instance of aa, not the fifth one. If we refresh the webpage at this point, the page will re-render the todos in the following order from bottom to top: bb, cc, dd, aa, bb, cc, dd, which is not what we expected (aa, bb, cc, dd, bb, cc, dd).

To address this issue, I've made a simple modification by adding an id to each todo item, resulting in a structure like: {"todo":[{"id":0,"value":"aa"},{"id":1,"value":"bb"},{"id":2,"value":"cc"},{"id":3,"value":"dd"},{"id":4,"value":"aa"},{"id":5,"value":"bb"},{"id":6,"value":"cc"},{"id":7,"value":"dd"}],"completed":[]}

I've also associated each todo's id with its DOM component. This way, when a component is clicked for deletion, we can retrieve the id from the component, find the corresponding record in todoList, and delete it accurately.

This is the description of the PR I wish to submit. Thank you.
